overview: Black fianchettoes at once and keeps options between ...c5, ...e5 and ...d6/...Nf6 for a King's Indian or Modern set-up. White develops with Nc3 and g3 or e4, aiming to build a centre or play in the English way. Often transposes to the Symmetrical English, King's Indian or Modern Defence.

white_ideas.idea: Nc3, e4 and d4 for a big centre, or g3 and Bg2 English style
Keep options of Nf3 and a Réti or Maróczy set-up

black_ideas.idea: ...Bg7, ...d6, ...e5 or ...c5 with a hypermodern attack on the centre
Wait to see White's set-up before choosing

typical_structures.structure: King's Indian-type or Symmetrical English with both bishops on long diagonals

character.notes: Flank opening, slow and strategic with transposition possibilities.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2.e4
sublines_that_differ.how: Transposes to a Modern Defence with White's big centre.

character.reason: Flexible hypermodern play without forced lines.

structure.reason: Flank opening, centre still undecided, like the English anchor.

plans.reason: Black fianchettoes and attacks the centre afterwards.
